title: Modi and Macron Will Unveil 120 Indian Deep-Tech Startups in Nice Tomorrow. Nothing Like This Has Happened Before.
excerpt: Bharat Innovates 2026, the first showcase of its kind, brings startups from IITs, IISc and BITS Pilani to 500 global investors across 13 sectors. Twenty-eight MoUs are expected on day one.
body:
When Prime Minister Narendra Modi and French President Emmanuel Macron step onto the stage at the Palais des Expositions in Nice on June 14, they will jointly inaugurate the most ambitious showcase India has ever mounted for its deep-tech ecosystem. Bharat Innovates 2026, a three-day event running through June 16, will put 120 Indian startups in front of more than 500 global investors, venture capital firms, and industry leaders — with $20 million in commitments already lined up and 28 innovation-focused memorandums of understanding expected to be signed on the opening day.

The startups were selected from over 3,000 applicants by a Technical Oversight Committee headed by Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India. They span 13 sectors: advanced computing, semiconductors, space technology, biotechnology, energy, healthcare, manufacturing, quantum computing, defence, and more. Collectively, these companies hold over 1,500 patents, have raised more than $1.5 billion in funding, and include established names like drone maker ideaForge and electric vehicle pioneer Ather Energy alongside early-stage ventures emerging from IIT, IISc and BITS Pilani incubators.

Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, who unveiled two strategic documents ahead of the event — the Bharat Innovates Startup Compendium and a portfolio of 50 cutting-edge research projects from premier institutions — described the initiative as a direct pathway connecting Indian innovators with international investment firms managing assets worth over $3 trillion and representing more than 12,000 investments worldwide.

"Bharat Innovates is creating strategic opportunities for collaboration between startups, academia and global investors," Pradhan said, adding that roadshows in Paris, Tokyo and Bengaluru had already generated strong investor interest.

The event is not just a pitch day. Its architecture includes an Incubator Innovation Bridge and an Industry Innovation Bridge — structured mechanisms designed to connect Indian founders with global corporations, research institutions, and startup ecosystems for long-term partnerships. The 28 MoUs to be signed cover collaborations with French and other international partners across research, commercialisation, and technology transfer.

The timing is deliberate. Bharat Innovates 2026 is a centrepiece of the India-France Year of Innovation, a diplomatic framework that has elevated the bilateral relationship to a Special Global Strategic Partnership. Modi is expected to be accompanied by External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, underscoring the government's intent to make this more than a symbolic exercise.

For India, the showcase represents a structural shift. The country's startup ecosystem — the world's third-largest by number of unicorns — has long been defined by consumer internet companies. Bharat Innovates pivots the narrative toward deep tech: the capital-intensive, research-heavy sectors where India has traditionally been a consumer of foreign innovation rather than an exporter of it.

The broader context makes this bet more consequential. India's digital public infrastructure — the JAM Trinity, UPI, India Stack — has already produced a $200 billion digitally delivered services trade surplus. The WTO's recent 244-page Trade Policy Review noted that India's digitally delivered services grew at 17.3% annually between 2021 and 2025. Manufacturing is the next frontier, and deep tech is the bridge.

For NRIs in Europe, the event opens a rare window. Indian-origin investors and entrepreneurs on the continent will have direct access to vetted deep-tech ventures — many still at stages where strategic capital and domain expertise from the diaspora could prove decisive. The MoUs on research collaboration could also create pathways for diaspora professionals in AI, biotech and semiconductors to engage with India's expanding institutional ecosystem.

Modi departs for Nice today, beginning a six-day European tour that will take him to Slovakia for the first-ever Indian prime ministerial visit, then to the G7 Summit in Evian, and finally to Paris for the VivaTech technology conference. But it is in Nice where the most consequential announcement of the trip may land — not in a bilateral communiqué, but in the deals signed between Indian founders and the global investors sitting across from them.
